summary.text: An Arthur Hills course from 2001 that mixes umbrella-pine woodland, dunes and open coastal holes beside the Atlantic near Cascais.

setting.text: Sits in the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, at the western end of the Estoril coast, with views of the Atlantic, the Sintra mountains and Cabo da Roca.
The club describes three landscapes on one course: umbrella pines, sand dunes and open coastal ground.
Top100golfcourses says the first four holes are tree-lined, the next twelve have more of a links feel with sandy ground and dunes, and the last two go back into the trees.
The routing is old-fashioned out-and-back, in the style of a classic Scottish links.
Hills said the umbrella pines on much of the outward nine were planted more than 70 years ago, and the dunes were preserved by the landowning family over generations.
Cabo da Roca, the westernmost point of mainland Europe, can be seen from the course.
Top100golfcourses says the greens are always firm and fast and full of slopes and borrows.

history.text: Opened in September 2001, designed by Arthur Hills.
Carlos Montez Champalimaud began developing this stretch of coast, now Quinta da Marinha, in the 1920s. His family also owns The Oitavos Hotel.
Top100golfcourses says Oitavos is one of only two European courses to carry the name of Arthur Hills, whose work is mostly in the USA.
The club says Hills is a past president of the American Society of Golf Course Architects and has designed more than 200 new courses.
The Open de Portugal list shows Oitavos as the venue in 2005 (Paul Broadhurst), 2007 (Pablo Martin), 2008 (Gregory Bourdy, after a playoff) and 2009 (Michael Hoey, after a playoff).
Top100golfcourses says it was the first golf course in Europe to receive Audubon Gold Certification.
Visit Lisboa says it was the first course in Europe and second in the world to gain Audubon International's Gold Signature Sanctuary status.

trivia.text: The club says it is the only Portuguese course ever ranked in Golf Magazine's world Top 100, and lists it as a Top 100 course in 2017/18.
Visit Lisboa says Golf Magazine ranked it 58th in the world in 2015.
Pioneer Golf says Golf Magazine ranked it 55th in the world in 2017.
In Top100golfcourses' 2026 Top 50 for Portugal, Oitavos Dunes sits inside the top eight.
The club says it became a Platinum Club of the World in 2015.
Visit Lisboa lists the course record as 63.
The club quotes Golf Magazine's Joe Passov calling it 'simply world class, my favourite in Europe'.
In a 'Review of the Month' on Top100golfcourses (November 2018), a reviewer said it looks like a links but plays more parkland, with no run on the fairways and greens that hold.
Top100golfcourses calls it a par 71 of just over 6,300 metres from the competition tees.

1.text: The club describes a broad landing area framed by umbrella pines, with the green set in a natural bowl of dunes.

2.text: The club calls it a short par four with a bunker in the middle of the landing area and a perched green.

3.text: The club says the 3rd is the first of five par threes, set in the pine forest, with three deep bunkers across the front of a long green.

4.text: The club says a north wind can change this short par four dramatically, and the quick green slopes towards the ocean.

5.text: The club calls it a long par four that usually plays into the prevailing wind, with a low green that suits a running approach.

7.text: The club says the 7th and 8th are back-to-back par fives, and that par is a good score on the 7th.

8.text: The tee shot plays uphill and the narrow, uphill approach goes to a small green among native dunes.
Top100golfcourses calls it the hardest hole on the course.

9.text: The club says this downhill par three faces the open landscape, with the mountains and Cabo da Roca behind, and the wind demands extra clubs.

14.text: Top100golfcourses calls the 14th probably the signature hole, a par three that can play longer than it looks, with the tee shot across a storm ravine that runs down the right.
The club says the 14th is set against one of the best views in golf, with the wind calling for a low shot over a deep sandy bunker.

15.text: The club says this par three plays downwind, with a gentle tier splitting the front and back of the green. It rates the 14th and 15th together among the best par threes around.

16.text: The club calls it the last of the par fives, with elevated tees and views of the ocean in the distance.

17.text: Top100golfcourses says the 17th is slightly easier than the 18th, with a downhill approach to a tricky green and a bunker front left to avoid.

18.text: The club calls it one of the best finishing par fours in Europe, played from elevated tees over pines to an elevated green.
Top100golfcourses describes a left dogleg with a narrow fairway.

local.text: Cascais, a pretty coastal town with a marina, is a short distance away. Guincho beach nearby is known for surfing.
Sintra, a long-time royal retreat now part of a UNESCO World Heritage site, is close by.
The club is about 20 minutes west of Lisbon and its airport.
